claims.text: What the strip looks like An early P wave with abnormal morphology, usually followed by a narrow QRS.
claims.quote: Premature Atrial Contraction (PAC): Early P wave with abnormal morphology, usually followed by a narrow QRS.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Timing: premature — the beat comes early
claims.quote: A premature atrial complex (PAC) is a premature beat

claims.text: P wave: abnormal — typically a different morphology and axis from the sinus P waves
claims.quote: The P wave typically has a different morphology and axis to the sinus P waves

claims.text: Hidden P wave: may sit in the preceding T wave, giving a “peaked” or “camel hump” T
claims.quote: The abnormal P wave may be hidden in the preceding T wave, producing a “peaked” or “camel hump” appearance

claims.text: PR interval: low atrial PACs give an inverted P wave with a relatively short PR, still ≥ 120 ms
claims.quote: PACs arising close to the AV node (“low atrial” ectopics) cause retrograde activation of the atria, producing an inverted P wave with a relatively short PR interval ≥ 120 ms
Abnormal (non-sinus) P wave usually followed by a normal QRS complex (< 120 ms)

claims.text: Aberrant or blocked PACs: may conduct aberrantly (usually RBBB morphology) or not at all; the P wave is still visible in both cases
claims.quote: PACs may also be conducted aberrantly (usually RBBB morphology), or not conducted at all. P waves will still be visible in both cases

claims.text: Pause after: a post-extrasystolic pause may follow, because a PAC that reaches the SA node resets it
claims.quote: Post-extrasystolic pauses may be present — PACs that reach the SA node may depolarise it, causing the SA node to be “reset”

claims.text: Unlike after a PVC, the pause is not equal to double the preceding R-R interval
claims.quote: Unlike with a premature ventricular complexe (PVC), the post-extrasystolic pause is not equal to double the preceding RR interval

claims.text: Patterns: bigeminy (every other beat), trigeminy (every third beat), quadrigeminy (every fourth beat), couplet (two in a row), triplet (three in a row)
claims.quote: Bigeminy — every other beat is a PAC Trigeminy — every third beat is a PAC Quadrigeminy — every fourth beat is a PAC Couplet – two consecutive PACs Triplet — three consecutive PACs

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: an ectopic focus fires early enough — before the next sinus impulse arrives — to capture the ventricles
claims.quote: However, if an ectopic focus depolarises early enough — before the arrival of the next sinus impulse — it may “capture” the ventricles, producing a premature contraction

claims.text: Frequent or symptomatic PACs: anxiety, sympathomimetics, beta-agonists, excess caffeine, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, digoxin toxicity, myocardial ischemia
claims.quote: Frequent or symptomatic PACs may occur due to: Anxiety Sympathomimetics Beta-agonists Excess caffeine Hypokalaemia Hypomagnesaemia Digoxin toxicity Myocardial ischaemia

claims.text: Occur in normal hearts, with or without precipitants (e.g., caffeine, alcohol, pseudoephedrine), or as a sign of cardiopulmonary disease; common in COPD
claims.quote: They may occur in normal hearts with or without precipitating factors (eg, caffeine, alcohol, pseudoephedrine) or may be a sign of a cardiopulmonary disorder. They are common in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

claims.text: In predisposed patients (e.g., left atrial enlargement, ischemic heart disease, WPW), a PAC can trigger a re-entry tachyarrhythmia — AF, flutter, AVNRT, AVRT
claims.quote: In patients with underlying predispositions (e.g. left atrial enlargement, ischaemic heart disease, WPW), a PAC may be the trigger for the onset of a re-entry tachyarrhythmia — e.g. Atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, AVNRT, AVRT

claims.text: Symptoms Frequent PACs: palpitations and a sense of the heart “skipping a beat”
claims.quote: Frequent PACs may cause palpitations and a sense of the heart “skipping a beat”

claims.text: Significance Occasional PACs in healthy people are generally benign; frequent PACs are associated with higher risk of stroke, all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, and AF
claims.quote: Occasional APBs in apparently healthy people are generally considered benign, and nearly everyone has some. Frequent APBs have been shown to be associated with an increased risk of stroke, of all-cause mortality, of cardiovascular mortality, and atrial fibrillation

claims.text: Treatment A normal electrophysiological phenomenon — usually no investigation or treatment needed
claims.quote: PACs are a normal electrophysiological phenomenon not usually requiring investigation or treatment
